feedback: This candidate continues the cautious tuning trend by further lowering base_speed to 0.7 and switching the line loss strategy from 'last_direction' to 'search_left', which actively steers the robot to the right when the line is lost. This change aims to improve recovery from line loss events, which have been frequent and caused stalling on the slalom track in all previous candidates (Iterations 0-4). The derivative gain kd is reduced to 0.3 to further dampen steering oscillations, which have remained moderately high despite earlier reductions (Iterations 3-4). The integral gain ki remains at 2.0 to maintain strong steady-state error correction, helping reduce rms_error and line loss events. The geometry and sensor layout remain unchanged, consistent with prior stable designs (Iterations 0-4). Depending on the next race results, if stalling persists on the slalom track, consider further lowering base_speed or experimenting with the line loss strategy to 'search_right' to test the opposite recovery direction. If steering oscillation remains high, consider reducing kd further or adjusting sensor_weights to reduce overcorrection. If rms_error or line loss events remain elevated, consider increasing ki slightly or refining sensor_weights. This candidate is a cautious refinement worth racing to gather telemetry for more targeted tuning.
requested_changes: controller.kd=0.2 if steering oscillation remains high
controller.ki=2.5 if rms_error or line loss events remain elevated
controller.base_speed=0.6 if stalling persists on slalom track
